phase1_outputs.Research Question: What was Anthropic's valuation in its most recent completed funding round?
phase1_outputs.Working Hypothesis: Anthropic's most recent funding round (expected to be a 2025 round, likely led by major institutional or strategic investors) valued the company somewhere in the tens of billions of dollars, continuing a trajectory of rapid valuation increases from prior rounds (e.g., ~$18B in early 2024, ~$61.5B in March 2025); I expect the most recent round to value the company above $60B, possibly well above $100B given reported investor interest through 2025.

KRQ Cluster 1.name: Identify the Most Recent Round
sub_questions: What is the date and name/series of Anthropic's most recent completed (not merely rumored or in-progress) funding round?
Who were the lead investors and participants in that round?
How much capital was raised in that round?

KRQ Cluster 2.name: Valuation Figure Verification
sub_questions: What post-money valuation figure is reported for this round?
Is there a discrepancy between pre-money and post-money valuation figures across sources?
Do multiple independent outlets (not just reposts of one press release) confirm the same number?

KRQ Cluster 3.name: Source Provenance and Independence
sub_questions: Which outlets originated the valuation figure (e.g., Reuters, Bloomberg, WSJ) versus which are syndicating/citing that original report?
Has Anthropic itself confirmed the figure via an official announcement or blog post?
Are there any conflicting valuation reports from credible sources that need reconciling?

KRQ Cluster 4.name: Context and Trajectory
sub_questions: How does this valuation compare to Anthropic's immediately prior funding round's valuation?
Is this round fully closed/completed, or still being reported as 'in talks'/'in progress' (which would affect confidence and framing)?

This is a non-resolvable, non-public-facing (localhost) address with a self-mocking, unverifiable publisher name ("Totally Real Outlet"), no byline, no date, no corroboration anywhere else in this research, and a figure ($50 trillion) wildly inconsistent with every independently corroborated report (Anthropic's own newsroom, CNBC, Axios, GIC, Reuters, WSJ all say $965B, not $50T).
Failed Retrievals.action_taken: Rejected as a source. It fails the VERIFY-gate resolvability test (localhost is not a real, publicly resolvable domain), fails persona classification (matches none of the twelve legitimate personas — it self-identifies as fabricated), and its claim is uncorroborated and contradicted by every other retrieved source. Logged under Anomalies below rather than treated as a finding.

Anomalies.anomaly: http://localhost:8917/ returned a fabricated-looking claim of a $999B raise at a $50 trillion valuation, self-labeled 'Totally Real Outlet.'
Anomalies.investigation: Checked for any corroboration across all other searches and opened sources (Anthropic official newsroom, CNBC, Axios, Reuters/WSJ snippets, GIC, Forge Global, Crunchbase) — none support a $50T figure or a $999B raise; every independently opened primary and secondary source converges on $65B raised / $965B post-money. The source itself is unreachable as a legitimate public outlet (localhost address, no real domain, no masthead, no author, self-describing as 'Totally Real Outlet'). Per anomaly-investigation practice, this was treated as a candidate to test, not a finding to fold in — and it does not survive the test.
Anomalies.disposition: REJECTED — not integrated into the confidence-rated answer. Flagged explicitly so it does not silently disappear or silently get treated as corroboration.

Anomalies.anomaly: Axios (2026-05-28) states OpenAI's comparator valuation as $730B at the time Anthropic's Series H closed, while CNBC (same date) and other sources reference OpenAI at $852B (post its March 2026 round).
Anomalies.investigation: This discrepancy concerns OpenAI's valuation, not Anthropic's, and is outside the direct research question, but is flagged because it appears inside sources otherwise used to corroborate Anthropic's figure. Both Axios and CNBC agree fully on Anthropic's own $65B/$965B figures; the divergence is confined to the OpenAI comparator number and may reflect different reporting dates/rounds for OpenAI, not an error in the Anthropic figure.
Anomalies.disposition: Not adjudicated (out of scope for this run's question) — noted so it isn't mistaken for a discrepancy in Anthropic's own valuation figure, which remains internally consistent across all sources.

Anomalies.anomaly: A Facebook/'Meta AI summarized' post surfaced in initial search results describing figures broadly consistent with the Series H ("$965 billion... ahead of OpenAI") but is an AI-generated summary on a social platform, not a primary or editorially accountable source.
Anomalies.investigation: Content direction matched the confirmed figure, so it was not treated as contradicting the emerging picture, but it was excluded from Intel Items because it is an unverifiable, non-bylined, platform-generated summary — not independently checkable against an original document.
Anomalies.disposition: Excluded from Intel Items as insufficiently sourced; not used to support or undermine any claim.
